361: C is correct because Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) delivers microsecond latency for caching reads of frequently accessed gaming data, meeting the sub-millisecond requirement. DynamoDB table export moves the historical data to Amazon S3 without building custom scripts, and Amazon Athena can then run one-time serverless queries on that data. All these services are fully managed, which keeps operational overhead low.
362: B and E are correct. B is correct because Kinesis Data Streams with the payment ID as the partition key guarantees that all records sharing the same key are written to the same shard and are received strictly in the order they were sent. E is correct because an Amazon SQS FIFO queue with the payment ID set as the message group ID ensures that messages within the same group are delivered exactly once and in order, preserving per-payment sequencing.
363: B is correct because Amazon SNS FIFO topics provide message ordering and deduplication while fanning out each unique event concurrently to multiple subscribers, which is exactly what is needed to feed the separate leaderboard, matchmaking, and authentication services. Standard SNS and EventBridge do not guarantee ordering across deliveries, and SQS FIFO queues are point-to-point and cannot deliver a single event to multiple consumers concurrently.
364: B and D are correct. B is correct because turning on server-side encryption on the SNS components with a KMS customer managed key, combined with a key policy that restricts usage to authorized principals, protects notifications at rest and limits who can use the key. D is correct because applying the same KMS customer managed key encryption with a restrictive key policy to the SQS queues protects data at rest, and setting a condition in the queue policy that requires encrypted connections over TLS protects the data in transit.
365: C is correct because RDS automated backups enable point-in-time recovery, allowing the database to be restored to any second within the retention period, which can be set up to 35 days. This satisfies the requirement to restore to the state from 5 minutes before an accidental change within the last 30 days. Snapshots, read replicas, and Multi-AZ deployments do not provide granular point-in-time restore capability.
366: D is correct because API Gateway usage plans with API keys let you identify and control which clients can access specific stages and routes of the API, making it straightforward to restrict premium content to subscribed users. This is a native API Gateway capability, so it requires minimal operational overhead compared to building custom filtering logic.
367: A is correct because AWS Global Accelerator uses static anycast IP addresses and the AWS global network edge locations to route user traffic to the closest healthy endpoint, improving both performance and availability for a global application. Network Load Balancers support UDP traffic and can target the on-premises servers, and because the application itself stays on premises, this design remains compliant. CloudFront cannot proxy UDP origins, and ALBs are not appropriate for UDP workloads in this design.
368: A is correct because an AWS account-level IAM password policy is the built-in mechanism that enforces complexity requirements, minimum length, and mandatory password rotation periods for all IAM users, including new users automatically. There is no per-user password policy in IAM, so the account-wide policy is the intended solution.
369: A is correct because AWS Batch runs jobs as containers or executables regardless of the programming language, which suits tasks written by different teams with no common language. It dynamically provisions and scales the compute environment based on the queued jobs, addressing the performance and scalability concerns, and scheduling with Amazon EventBridge is simple and fully managed, keeping operational overhead low.
370: C is correct because a NAT gateway is an AWS-managed service placed in a public subnet that allows EC2 instances in private subnets to initiate outbound connections to the internet, such as to the license server, while remaining fully managed and highly available. This minimizes operational maintenance compared to a self-managed NAT instance, and a NAT gateway must reside in a public subnet to function.
371: C and D are correct. C is correct because enabling EBS encryption by default in the Region with the customer managed KMS key selected ensures that every EBS volume created for the managed node group is automatically encrypted with that key, with no manual volume-by-volume work. D is correct because the EKS cluster needs an IAM role with a policy that grants permission to use the customer managed key, allowing KMS to create the grants required for cluster and node group EBS volume encryption.
372: B is correct because storing the high-resolution images in Amazon S3 provides durable, highly available, and cost-effective object storage that scales effortlessly to millions of images and heavy update bursts. Using DynamoDB with the geographic code as the key and the S3 URL as the value gives single-digit millisecond performance, automatic scaling of throughput, and a one-to-one mapping between each code and its image. This combination avoids the cost and scalability limits of pushing large binary blobs through a relational database.
373: D is correct because the access pattern is well known: data is used daily for retraining during the first 30 days, accessed only quarterly for analysis until 12 months, and then archived. S3 Standard provides immediate low-latency access for the daily retraining workload, transitioning to Standard-IA after 30 days minimizes cost for the quarterly analysis, and moving to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year provides the lowest-cost archival retention. Because the pattern is predictable, a lifecycle policy is more cost-effective than paying Intelligent-Tiering monitoring fees.
374: D is correct because a single AWS Direct Connect connection provides a dedicated, consistent, low-latency link that can reliably carry hundreds of gigabytes of data daily to the latency-sensitive on-premises application, and it avoids paying for three separate connections. A transit gateway attached to all three VPCs enables inter-VPC communication and connects them to the on-premises data center through that one Direct Connect link, maximizing cost-effectiveness.
375: A is correct because AWS Step Functions is a fully managed serverless orchestrator that can sequence multiple Lambda functions into a responsive workflow, coordinate tasks running on EC2 instances, containers, and on-premises servers, and support manual approval steps through its wait-for-callback pattern. This built-in orchestration with visual workflows and error handling meets the order-processing requirements with minimal operational overhead.
376: A is correct because RDS Proxy is a fully managed connection pooling service that multiplexes many application connections onto fewer database connections, preventing the connection exhaustion errors that serverless applications cause during demand spikes. By placing applications behind RDS Proxy, connection handling is offloaded to AWS with minimal changes and no infrastructure for the company to maintain.
377: B is correct because EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks pause instances during launch and terminate transitions and can trigger a custom script, via Amazon EventBridge or Amazon SQS notifications, to report the instance data to the auditing system precisely when instances come online or are being removed. This event-driven approach reacts immediately to every instance change without polling, making it the most efficient option.
378: B is correct because a Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and supports UDP traffic, and it integrates with Auto Scaling so game servers automatically scale during anticipated daily demand spikes. Amazon DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode automatically scales read and write throughput up and down in response to traffic, so the non-relational gamer score data scales without any manual intervention.
379: B is correct because provisioned concurrency keeps a set number of Lambda execution environments initialized and warm, so requests do not suffer cold starts, and the expensive library loading and database connection setup happens in advance. This directly reduces response latency for all users with only a simple configuration change and no architectural changes to the company's operations.
380: D is correct because an AWS Lambda function invoked on a schedule by Amazon EventBridge can call the start and stop APIs for both the EC2 instances and RDS DB instances outside of business hours, eliminating idle-time compute costs. This serverless approach requires no additional infrastructure to run or maintain, minimizing cost and infrastructure maintenance compared to cron-based or third-party alternatives.
